newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis worried about security, poll shows.
newsitem.headline: Israelis worried about security, poll shows.

text.p: An opinion poll published on Friday about security showed four out of five Israelis were worried about security following a Washington summit this week called to end Israeli-Palestinian violence.

The Dahaf Institute poll for the daily Yedioth Ahronoth showed 79 percent were worried -- 51 percent of those polled "very worried" -- about the security situation following a White House summit this week called to end Arab-Israeli violence.
Right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, 46, ousted Labour party leader Shimon Peres four months ago on a promise to pursue peace while better guarding Israeli security.

The poll showed Israelis were split on whether Netanyahu's meeting in Washington with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was a success. Of the 502 people interviewed, 46 percent said yes, 48 percent no and the rest had no response.

Of those who voted for Netanyahu, 37 percent said the summit had failed. The poll, conducted on Thursday, had a four percent margin of error. It did not elaborate on what those questioned would view as a successful summit.
Fifty-eight Palestinians and 15 Israelis died last week in clashes and gunbattles unprecedented in the three years since a landmark Israeli-PLO peace deal.
